questions.q: What specific detail triggers the second argument between Lomov and Natalya?
questions.a: Lomov mentions that his dog Guess has gone lame, and Natalya contradicts him by claiming Squeezer is a better dog. A wrong answer (e.g., "they argue over the meadows again" or "Chubukov starts it") reveals the student cannot distinguish the two arguments or identify the textual trigger.

questions.q: Explain how the argument shifts from an objective comparison of the dogs to a subjective, personal quarrel. Use one example from each stage.
questions.a: Stage 1 (objective): Lomov cites Guess's price (125 roubles), pedigree, and performance in a hunt. Stage 2 (subjective): Natalya calls Guess "old" and "ugly," Lomov calls Squeezer "overshot" and a "bad hunter." Stage 3 (personal): Lomov calls Natalya a "blind hen," she calls him an "intriguer." A wrong answer that only lists insults misses the structural escalation Chekhov builds.

questions.q: Lomov claims Guess is "a first-rate dog" because he "went for 125 roubles" and "is a thoroughbred." Natalya counters that Squeezer cost 85 roubles but is "a hundred times better." Apply the concept of *flawed evidence* to explain why both arguments fail to prove superiority.
questions.a: Price ≠ quality (Guess cost more but is lame; Squeezer cheaper but untested). Pedigree ≠ current ability (Guess is thoroughbred but old; Squeezer's parentage is cited but not performance). Hunt anecdotes are selective: Lomov recalls one success; Natalya recalls one failure. Both ignore the other's evidence. A wrong answer that says "Lomov is right because he paid more" shows inability to evaluate evidence critically.

questions.q: Analyze the dramatic irony in this argument: the audience knows the proposal is the real purpose, but the characters don't act on it. How does Chekhov structure the dialogue to heighten this irony?
questions.a: Chekhov uses three techniques: (1) Interruption — just as Lomov tries to propose ("Natalya Stepanovna, I..."), the dog topic hijacks him. (2) Escalation — each reply raises the emotional stakes, pushing the proposal further away. (3) Chubukov's entrance — he joins the dog fight instead of nudging the proposal. A wrong answer that only defines dramatic irony without linking to dialogue structure misses the playwright's craft.

questions.q: Evaluate the claim: "The dog argument is more revealing of Lomov and Natalya's characters than the meadow argument." Defend your position with textual evidence.
questions.a: Yes. The meadow argument was about property — external, legalistic. The dog argument is about *taste, judgment, and ego* — internal, personal. Lomov's hypochondria surfaces ("palpitations," "nerves") when his expertise is challenged. Natalya's stubbornness shifts from legal right to aesthetic opinion. Both expose insecurity masked as superiority. A wrong answer that says "both are just petty" fails to differentiate the *nature* of the pettiness.

questions.q: Write a 4-line dialogue snippet where Lomov and Natalya argue about a modern equivalent (e.g., smartphones, bikes) that mirrors the structure: fact → opinion → insult. Keep their voices recognizable.
questions.a:
Lomov: My iPhone 15 cost 80,000 — A16 chip, 48MP camera.  
Natalya: My Pixel 8 was 60,000 and takes better low-light shots — your photos are oversaturated.  
Lomov: Oversaturated? Your screen has a green tint — you're blind to colour accuracy.  
Natalya: And you're a tech snob who thinks price equals quality — typical Lomov logic.  
A poor answer uses generic insults ("you're stupid") without preserving the fact-opinion-insult progression or character voices.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The second argument in *The Proposal* is a comic quarrel between Lomov and Natalya over the ______ of their respective hunting dogs — Lomov's "Guess" and Natalya's "Squeezer" — which escalates from a casual comparison into a vicious personal attack, revealing how trivial ego-driven disputes derail the marriage proposal.

Fill in the blank: Imagine you're watching two neighbours argue over whose phone has a ______ camera — they start with megapixels, end up insulting each other's grandparents, and forget they were supposed to discuss a wedding.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can trace the argument's progression from technical comparison to personal insult, identify the dramatic irony that the proposal is forgotten, and explain how Chekhov uses the dog dispute to satirize the landed gentry's misplaced pride and pettiness.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Imagine you're watching two neighbours argue over whose phone has a better camera — they start with megapixels, end up insulting each other's ______, and forget they were supposed to discuss a wedding.
